svg.aria-label: What a stream stack trace actually looks like, captured by actually running the failure. Left: an NPE thrown inside rate() while mapping over card deposits via deposits.stream().map(...).reduce(...) produces nine frames: rate, a synthetic lambda dollar process dollar 0 frame for the lambda passed to map, ReferencePipeline dollar 3 dollar 1 dot accept which is the sink stage wrapping the lambda, AbstractPipeline dot copyInto which drives the loop over the source, wrapAndCopyInto, ReduceOps evaluateSequential, AbstractPipeline evaluate, ReferencePipeline reduce, and process. Right: the same failure written as an explicit for loop produces exactly four frames: rate, processLoop, process, main. A note explains that a long method-reference-heavy pipeline combined with recursion and flatMap risks StackOverflowError because each stage nests another call frame before the source is ever pulled.
svg.text: WHAT A STREAM STACK TRACE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE
STREAM — deposits.stream().map(d -> ...rate(d)).reduce(...)
CardDeposit("DEP-301", 65.00) — rate() hits a null currency lookup
captured live: javac/java 25, --release 21 unavailable on this JVM
NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.length()"
at Example.rate(Example.java:16)
frame 1 — where the NPE is actually thrown
at Example.lambda$process$0(Example.java:9)
frame 2 — synthetic: the compiler-generated body for d -> ...
at ReferencePipeline$3$1.accept(ReferencePipeline.java:214)
frame 3 — the map stage's Sink, invoking the lambda per element
at Collections$2.tryAdvance(Collections.java:5182)
frame 4 — the backing List's Spliterator pulling one element
at Collections$2.forEachRemaining(Collections.java:5190)
frame 5 — spliterator driving the remaining elements
at AbstractPipeline.copyInto(AbstractPipeline.java:570)
frame 6 — pushes source elements through the Sink chain
at AbstractPipeline.wrapAndCopyInto(...:560)
frame 7 — wraps the terminal Sink around the stage chain
at ReduceOps$ReduceOp.evaluateSequential(...:921)
frame 8 — the reduce terminal op's sequential evaluator
at AbstractPipeline.evaluate(AbstractPipeline.java:265)
frame 9 — dispatches to the terminal op's evaluator
at ReferencePipeline.reduce(ReferencePipeline.java:693)
frame 10 — the public reduce() call site
at Example.process(Example.java:10) / main(:29)
frame 11–12 — your code, top and bottom of the pipeline setup
12 frames total for one map + one reduce
6 of them are stream machinery, not your code
FOR LOOP — same NullPointerException, same rate() call
processLoop iterates CardDeposit rows directly
no pipeline stages, no synthetic frames
NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.length()"
at Example3.rate(Example3.java:9)
frame 1 — same throw site as the stream version
at Example3.processLoop(Example3.java:15)
frame 2 — the for loop body calling rate()
at Example3.process(Example3.java:21)
frame 3 — the caller that delegates to processLoop
at Example3.main(Example3.java:26)
frame 4 — entry point
4 frames total — exactly your call depth
no synthetic lambda frame, no pipeline machinery
Pitfall — StackOverflowError risk
A long method-chain pipeline (many .map/.filter stages) nests
one Sink.accept frame per stage before the source is ever pulled.
flatMap adds another nested sub-stream evaluation per element,
and any recursive call inside a mapping function multiplies that
depth further. A deep pipeline over 2,800,000 stake reservations
with a recursive scoring function inside flatMap is the shape that
exhausts the stack — the for-loop equivalent does not, because
its frame count is bounded by call depth, not pipeline stage count.
The failure mode is StackOverflowError, not a slow leak — it is immediate.
